description: The paper combines multiple thermal-load predictors in an expert system and compares the combined forecast with its individual methods. The methods include regression, tree models, neural networks and support-vector machines. The provider is Davy Geysen , Oscar De Somer , Christian Johansson , Jens Brage , Dirk Vanhoudt. Coverage: The evaluation uses 27 months of measurements from ten residential buildings in Rottne, Sweden, plus weather forecasts. Exact dates and sampling intervals are not established in the abstract. Access: The provider publishes a metadata page describing the resource and its access route. Resource files were not downloaded or executed. Licence and cost: The page does not establish a reuse licence or complete cost conditions. Provider confirmation is required before reuse. Limitations: The study’s validation is bounded to its supplied data. Public availability of the measurements and model code was not established. For simulation it provides a documented load-forecasting comparison for district-heating operation. Related resources: For comparison, model-pandapipes provides pipe-network modelling. This is a thematic link, not evidence of use in this study.
